<channel|>In a standard Transformer, every token in a sequence passes through every single parameter in the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) layers. As models grow to trillions of parameters, this becomes computationally unsustainable. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures solve this by replacing the dense FFN layers with a collection of specialized sub-networks, known as "experts."

The routing process begins with a **router** (a learned linear layer) that sits before the expert layer. For every incoming token, the router calculates a probability distribution across all available experts. Instead of activating all of them, the system employs **top-k routing**, where only the top one or two experts with the highest scores are selected for that specific token. The token is then sent only to those selected experts, while the remaining experts remain idle.
